# Visual Design Reviewer

**Explorer current location — APPROVE.** In both forced-color palettes the active file and folder previously inherited the same visual treatment as adjacent links once the system replaced the selection fill. The candidate underlines the current label at 2.25px from the text. A long file title remains legible line by line, including six lines at 900px. Moving keyboard focus adds the existing 2px ring, visually distinct from the persistent underline. The phone drawer and tablet and desktop rails retain the measured file row heights of 65, 138 and 75px respectively. The 450-weight file and 550-weight folder retain SN Pro and their original wrapping. Ordinary light and pure-black themes retain their selected fill and existing type. The rule is scoped to the Explorer's current-page mark and the forced-colors query. No candidate defect or preference change requested.

**Code and diagram Copy — APPROVE.** After moving across the mobile breakpoint twice, the baseline exposed three overlapping Copy targets. Shift+Tab traversed each of them in the diagram even though the icon occupied one position. The candidate retained keyboard focus on the original button through the round trip. Shift+Tab reached Expand and then left the group. The two newer buttons stayed measurable and hidden. The surviving icon was legible at rest, with an individual hover fill and a 2px keyboard outline. It occupied 44px on the touch phone and 32px in the fine-pointer cases. On an initialized diagram, Copy and Expand had a 4.8px horizontal gap. Expand was visible on touch at rest and by keyboard focus on the wider layouts. Activating Copy with Enter returned the expected 125-character PowerShell sample and 154-character diagram source from the clipboard in both themes. Code retained TX-02. The candidate restricts Copy transitions to the two paint colors and reduced motion computed to 0s. The correction stays in the existing technical-content rule; it relies on Quartz's documented-in-place prepending order. No candidate defect or preference change requested.

**Coverage.** I exercised both running builds in Chromium at 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels, with matching regular light, pure-black dark, white forced-color and black forced-color cases. I inspected Home, Blog, the long current article row, the Azure machine configuration code, and the Azure documentation diagrams. I opened Search, entered “azure”, used arrow selection and dismissed it. I followed the Blog listing to the article and returned, opened the Explorer drawer, and crossed the responsive breakpoint in both directions. Separately, a software-WebGL run rendered local and global graphs in the wider frames. Escape returned focus to the opener. The phone graph remained suppressed. The local graph edge tokens were #817d72 and #707070 across builds. The page measure, headline hierarchy, Search result structure and archive alignment held through these states.

**Scope of findings.** I reproduced Mermaid's existing syntax-error drawing after responsive rerender in both previews. Approval covers the exposed Copy and Expand presentation and interaction, including copying the original source in this state. The shared screenshot set also includes intermediate responsive states. The dedicated current-4242/current-4243 crops show the settled Explorer and agree with my independent captures. I found no new critical, material or minor visual defect in the proposed stylesheet.

# Independent Visual Design Reviewer, revised build 4244

## Current Explorer file and folder — APPROVE

On the frozen build, a current file and a current folder have the same resting treatment as the surrounding links when forced colors remove the selected fill. On the revision, a continuous underline distinguishes the current label. The 2.25px offset stays clear of the type on the two-line phone row and six-line tablet row. The separate 2px focus outline still identifies keyboard focus. Both light and dark high-contrast palettes preserve their system ink. In standard themes, the current row retained its established fill and typography. Current file and folder remained SN Pro at weights 450 and 550 respectively. The row heights, line breaks, indentation and neighboring entries matched the frozen build at every width. The style is limited to the Explorer’s current-page label in the forced-colors query. No candidate defect or visual preference change requested.

## Code Copy and diagram controls — APPROVE

I changed Chromium’s actual default font preference from 16px to 32px and back while an initialized diagram’s Expand control held keyboard focus. At each change I sampled 32 animation frames. The first implementation at 4243 overlapped Copy and Expand by as much as 33.20px on tablet and desktop, and 5.20px on the touch phone. The corrected build kept 4.80px of space at the original size and 9.59px at the enlarged size across both directions. Every sampled gap was positive in all six viewport/theme combinations. The two controls kept equal dimensions throughout. Both grew from 32px to 64px on fine-pointer layouts and from 44px to 48px on the phone. The dark and light focus rings remain wholly visible. None of these cases produced page-level horizontal overflow. The new transition list on the existing Expand selector addresses position and size directly while retaining the focus reveal.

After two responsive breakpoint crossings the frozen build exposed three Copy buttons. On the revision only the original was visible on the PowerShell block and the Mermaid source. The original kept focus through both crossings. Shift+Tab visited Expand and then left the group in all six forced-color cases. Its rest, hover and 2px keyboard focus treatments stayed legible in normal light and pure-black themes. The code remained TX-02. Enter copied the exact 125-character PowerShell sample and the 154-character diagram source at each width in each theme. Copy’s transition duration reached 0s under reduced motion. The existing Mermaid syntax-error drawing following a responsive rerender remains reproducible on both builds. It does not obstruct the source action. No new candidate defect or preference change requested.

## Surrounding site

I used the frozen and revised localhost previews at 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels, in light and pure-black dark modes, plus both forced-color palettes for the current Explorer states. I opened Home and Blog, followed the first listing to its article and returned, opened Search, entered “azure”, used keyboard selection and dismissed the dialog. I inspected the Azure machine configuration code, the Azure documentation diagram, and the long Microsoft Defender Explorer title. The articles retained their serif hierarchy and the archive kept its shared title edge and distinct metadata. Using software WebGL, the local and global graphs rendered in the wider layouts, Escape returned focus to the graph opener, and the phone graph remained suppressed. In light and dark themes the edge tokens remained #817d72 and #707070. I found no critical, material or minor visual regression in either candidate change.

## I — Responsive and Accessibility Reviewer

I tested the served baseline `index-530afd62.css` at :4242 and candidate `index-a3308b2a.css` at :4243. Chromium covered 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels in light and pure-black dark themes. I inspected the paired screenshots, opened the actual mobile drawer, followed Home → Blog → article, used search results with the keyboard, and opened and dismissed the desktop global graph. Escape restored both search and graph openers. The drawer made the main content inert and returned focus to its opener on Escape.

**Explorer current item — APPROVE.** In Chromium’s Windows forced-color emulation, the baseline rendered current and inactive links alike. The candidate visibly underlines the current Blog folder and current article in both palettes. A neighboring focused link independently received the 2px system focus outline. Moving focus onto the current link preserved both cues. The longest tested title used the same 2, 6 and 3 lines at the three widths on both builds, with no clipped label. The light and dark forced-color text ratios were 13.99:1 and 19.56:1. The media query uses the existing page-current semantics and leaves ordinary typography and spacing intact. No material regression.

**Copy targets and motion — APPROVE.** After two responsive reinitializations, the baseline exposed three Copy stops on a single code block. The candidate exposed one through keyboard traversal and the accessibility tree for ordinary code and Mermaid. The exact original focused DOM button stayed focused on both round trips, with a 2px outline. The normal fine-pointer target was 32px and the 390px touch target was 44px. The adjacent Mermaid Expand target had a 4.8px gap. An actual keyboard activation copied the exact authored PowerShell (125 characters) and Mermaid source (154 characters) across all six candidate cases. Touch activation also copied the expected text after resizing. SPA entry, Back and Forward completed on mobile and desktop and Copy still worked. The normal-state icon contrast was at least 6.26:1 across both themes. With a pointer hovering and browser font size doubled, the candidate changed 32→64px immediately. Only foreground/background color transitioned under normal motion, and the reduced-motion run recorded zero animations. The matching shell block also passed pointer-click clipboard verification.

Firefox 159 native page zoom at 200% and 400% yielded 720px and 360px effective viewports. Both themes retained TX-02 and contained long lines within the code scroller. At 400% the 471px sample scrolled in its 323px container. Neither page acquired horizontal overflow.

**Existing material defect.** On both builds, the Azure Application Gateway Mermaid diagram initially rendered correctly, then showed a syntax-error graphic following the 390→900→390 breakpoint sequence. The candidate preserved source copying and the separate Expand action. The shared renderer still requires its own fix. Quartz also continues to generate redundant hidden DOM buttons, which is a remaining implementation cost. The tests establish visible and keyboard behavior through emulation and native browser zoom. A physical Windows high-contrast environment and screen-reader speech were outside this assessment.

# Independent CSS and Quartz V5 review

**Decision — REVISE the combined stylesheet. APPROVE the Explorer change and REVISE the Copy transition change.** Compared the working SCSS and the two live, emitted builds. The Explorer gains a visible forced-colors current-page indicator. Repeated Quartz renders expose one usable Copy control per article code block, with stable keyboard focus and immediate geometry and outline changes. The Copy and Expand controls overlap briefly while the reader increases their font size.

| Change | Decision | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current file and current folder in forced colors | APPROVE | The current link alone changes from no decoration to an underline 2.25 CSS pixels below the text at the default navigation size. The indicator spans each line of a long title. File row heights were 65, 138 and 75px at 390, 900 and 1440px in both builds. Blog folder heights were 44, 33 and 33px. Neither normal palette acquires the underline. |
| One visible and accessible Copy control per code block, including its transitions | REVISE | After two graph-mode breakpoint crossings, the same code block exposed three Copy buttons in the baseline accessibility tree and one in the candidate tree. Starting on the original button, Shift+Tab previously landed on its duplicate and now reaches the preceding pre. The same focused DOM node survives both crossings. Both code and raw Mermaid source copied exactly. After navigating away and back using Quartz SPA, the newly bound button still copied the correct 125-character PowerShell block. |

## Source and cascade

- Compared the live `index-530afd62.css` and `index-a3308b2a.css`. The only emitted rule changes are the forced-colors current-page treatment, the Copy selector and its transition properties, sibling visibility, and reduced motion. The main asset grows by 391 bytes uncompressed. Component assets and browser script URLs agree.
- The Explorer selector uses the rendered `aria-current="page"` on the native file or folder link. The existing navigation observer owns that attribute and updates it on navigation. The rule adds no selected state to ancestors, adjacent items, the TOC or folder chevrons. Forced colors retain system ink, and the keyboard focus outline remains separate from selection.
- `.markdown-rendered pre > button.clipboard-button` has specificity (0,2,2). It wins against the later plugin rule `pre:hover > .clipboard-button` at (0,2,1), including while hovered. Copy changes from a blanket 0.2s transition to color and background-color only. Its computed reduced-motion transition is none, 0s. No additional important declaration or script change appears in this patch.
- The Clipboard plugin registers both nav and render callbacks. Each pass prepends another button, assigns the click handler to it, and registers listener cleanup for navigation. It captures the decoded clipboard data when available, otherwise the code text, and normalizes double newlines. The later sibling selector keeps the earliest button and uses visibility to exclude all the newer copies from hit testing, tab order and the accessibility tree. It relies on the plugin's current prepend order. The DOM elements and new click handlers still accumulate during repeated render events on the same document.
- The Mermaid plugin reads the first Copy element's offsetWidth and margins before writing the inline right offset to Expand and binding its action. Hidden duplicates still measure 32px at a desktop 16px root size. Holding the actual remote Mermaid module pending left Copy functional and Expand hidden. On release, a valid flowchart initialized, Expand became visible with inline right equal to calc(32px + 0.3rem), and the visual gap was 4.80px. The regular and reduced-motion Expand rules already exist outside this patch.

## Browser coverage

- Independent Chromium runs on both ports used 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels, light and pure-black dark palettes, no-preference and reduced motion, and forced-color emulation. Inspected Home, Blog folder, Setting Up Azure Machine Configuration, The Microsoft Azure Documentation, Increasing Disk Space on Linux Servers, Explorer, search for Azure with arrow navigation and Escape, Copy focus, hover and activation, diagrams, graph and wide-table edges.
- Compared the supplied code and diagram captures, and the additional current-file/current-folder pairs where Explorer was expanded. The initial paired desktop Explorer captures had a collapsed tree after resizing. The additional captures directly show the current items in all six width/palette combinations.
- Code still computes to TX-02. The wrappers retain local horizontal scrolling at 390px, with no page overflow in the tested layouts. On the Linux article the 591px table scrolls within 355px on the phone and the right-edge indicator clears at the end. Search retains its active option and returns keyboard focus to its opener. Home retains the warm-light and black surfaces with graph edge tokens #817d72 and #707070. The desktop graph opened to a live canvas and Escape restored focus to its trigger in both builds.
- Candidate and baseline both passed source-copy checks on the two distinct input paths. The candidate kept the original focused Copy inside an article after both breakpoint crossings across all six width/palette pairs. Click success feedback still blurs the clicked button through the existing plugin handler.

## Defects and limitations

- **Material transition regression needing a small correction.** With the first valid Azure diagram visible and Expand focused, increasing the root font size from 16px to 32px enlarges Copy immediately while Expand animates its width and right position. At 40ms the boxes overlap by 20.58px on the candidate. The baseline has 6.22px of clearance at the same time. Both controls have full opacity. Natural animation sampling also recorded a 23.7px overlap at 28ms and 3px at 75ms in the candidate. Both builds settle to 9.59px of clearance. Add `transition-property: opacity, color, background-color` to the existing Mermaid Expand owner rule to keep the hover fade and update its geometry alongside Copy. Retest a live root-size increase and decrease, hover, focus and reduced motion.

- **Material existing runtime defect.** After a valid Azure Application Gateway flowchart renders, changing 1440px to 390px fires Quartz's graph-mode render event. In both builds the Mermaid plugin reinitializes, reads the existing drawing's label text as fresh source, and produces an SVG reporting “Syntax error in text”. This reproduced on the first breakpoint crossing and persisted at 1440px after the return trip. The expanded overlay can consequently contain an error drawing. The presentation patch leaves source copying and the existing expansion offset intact. It does not repair diagram reinitialization or remove the accumulating buttons and handlers.
- Initial graph probes deliberately blocked non-Mermaid external resources and reached the existing graph fallback. Repeated the graph checks with normal resource loading and enabled Chromium software graphics. The live local and modal canvases initialized and closed correctly. Forced colors were emulated in Chromium.
- The recorded production build completed, all 164 tests passed and the SCSS formatter passed. The repository-wide type check still reports the historical micromorph and remark-parse/lib declaration failures. The prior review history records the same diagnostics on the baseline.

# Independent CSS and Quartz V5 reassessment

**APPROVE the revised stylesheet.** I reviewed the build using `index-0731cabb.css` at port 4244. I compared its browser behavior with the accepted baseline at 4242 and the superseded candidate at 4243.

| Change | Decision | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current Explorer file and folder in forced colors | **APPROVE** | In the light and dark forced palettes at 390, 900 and 1440px, the current anchor alone has an underline. The 2.25px offset is visible on individual lines of wrapped file titles and on the short Blog folder link. Both standard themes retain the existing weight, row height, fill and indentation. |
| One usable Copy control and coordinated diagram-control transitions | **APPROVE** | Following two graph-mode crossings, one of three Copy elements is exposed to hit testing, sequential keyboard focus and the accessibility tree. The original focused element survives. Copy and Expand retain independent target rectangles on every sampled frame while enlarging and shrinking text. |

## Responsive behavior and interaction

- Tested real Chromium at 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels, with light and pure-black dark themes, normal and reduced motion. Each combination used an initialized Azure Application Gateway flowchart while the root size changed from 16px to 32px and back. Across 24 font transitions, the revised file had 9.59px of clearance on every sampled frame at 32px and 4.80px at 16px. The superseded file reached −33.20px on enlargement and temporarily left 47.59px on shrink. The baseline moved both controls gradually and retained positive clearance.
- For each size change I clicked both physical button centers with Chromium’s mouse or touchscreen input. All 48 activations worked. Copy wrote the exact original text, Expand opened a valid flowchart, and Escape closed the overlay. A separate desktop test activated Expand within 37ms of enlargement and copied source within 14ms of shrinking.
- I held the Mermaid module pending to verify that Copy operates before initialization. Expand appeared after the existing inline readiness marker. On desktop its initial measured Copy width was 32px. After additional render events, the first, hidden Copy element still measured 32px and the original Copy retained focus. On a regular PowerShell block, Shift+Tab from the only exposed Copy reached the pre. The baseline landed on a second Copy. Navigating from the code article to another article and back via Quartz SPA left one functional Copy for the new content.
- Inspected Home, Blog, Setting Up Azure Machine Configuration, The Microsoft Azure Documentation and Increasing Disk Space on Linux Servers. Search for Azure, arrow selection, Escape and focus return worked, including a fresh mobile light-mode trial after the initial interaction raced initialization. The real graph canvas opened and returned focus on tablet and desktop, and was suppressed on mobile and with reduced motion. Phone tables scrolled from their start to end within the 355px box. TX-02 code, the established article typography, light page and pure-black dark page remained intact.

## Cascade and maintenance

The only emitted change since port 4243 adds a transition-property declaration to the existing Mermaid Expand rule. It limits transitions to opacity, color and background-color. Its owner selector wins over the later hover shorthand. Width, height, top and right now update together with Copy. The existing reduced-motion branch still computes to none and 0s. The rule introduces no new class, important declaration, marker, DOM update or script dependency.

The Explorer rule follows the aria-current value already maintained by the site, and only applies when the forced-colors query matches. Copy still relies on the plugin prepending new buttons, and the Mermaid plugin still measures the first Copy in DOM order. The CSS retains the original focused button and measurable geometry while suppressing duplicates from presentation.

## Defects and disposition

The material, candidate-introduced control overlap from the first review is resolved. No further stylesheet correction is required. Two existing runtime behaviors remain. Repeated renders can accumulate Copy DOM nodes and handlers, and graph-mode crossings can cause the Mermaid plugin to read rendered labels as fresh diagram source and display its error SVG on redraw. Both reproduce against the accepted baseline. Initial rendering, raw-source copying and target activation tested successfully. This independent verification used Chromium with emulated forced colors.

The final build emitted 913 files, all 164 tests passed, and the scoped formatter passed. The earlier repository-wide type check reported the same two known dependency declaration failures documented on the baseline.

director.assessment:
# Independent Design Director final assessment

**APPROVE the corrected stylesheet for the site's existing visual scope.** All three independent reviewers approved both changes after testing the revision. The earlier candidate earned a revision request for a material overlap between adjacent diagram controls during a live font change. The corrected stylesheet resolved it.

The accepted comparison on port 4242 served `index-530afd62.css`. The first candidate on port 4243 served `index-a3308b2a.css`. The corrected preview on port 4244 serves `index-0731cabb.css`.

| Cycle | Disposition and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 14 · Explorer and rail alignment | Retain the existing frame. Home title, archive title and article prose shared x=17.55, 221.5 and 382 CSS pixels at 390, 900 and 1440px in my final browser checks. The expanded tree measurements found zero misaligned continuation lines and zero lines outside their rows across both themes. The desktop graph and center header begin at y=63px. The article breadcrumb occupies the space before its large title. |
| 15 · Dark hierarchy | Retain solid `#ababab` secondary text and the pure-black page. On the black rail, secondary text measures 9.14:1, the current file measures 11.91:1 on its selection fill, and prose measures 19.26:1. In the matched comparisons `#999999` reduced legibility of long wrapped labels. The brighter `#b8b8b8` trial brought the right-hand rail closer to prose without improving selection or alignment. |
| 16 · Current page in forced colors | Approve the Explorer-only 0.15em underline. The baseline current file and folder lost their visual distinction under forced colors. The candidate marks the element already carrying the page-current attribute. Its underline persists independently of the keyboard outline. File rows measured 65, 138 and 75px across the three widths on both builds. No change in normal mode was warranted. |
| 17 · Copy across responsive initialization | Approve the corrected presentation of one Copy control per code block. After crossing the frame breakpoint twice, the old build exposed three buttons and the corrected build exposed one. The original button retained focus and copied the exact 154-character Mermaid source even after the diagram itself failed to rerender. PowerShell's 125-character sample also copied. Hidden buttons retain the dimensions the existing diagram initializer reads. The plugin continues to allocate button nodes and listeners. |
| 18 · Page reflow | The corpus check sampled all 161 nonredirect paths at 320, 801 and 1200px in reduced motion, with external requests and raster images blocked. No document overflow or changed horizontal bounds for main content or titles occurred in that matrix. Three-width, two-theme browser checks covered loaded fonts and ordinary Home, listing, article, navigation, search and graph states. Firefox native 200% and 400% zoom kept horizontal scrolling inside code. |
| 19 · SPA and history | Keep Quartz's existing current-page semantics. Chromium and Linux WebKit each reported the correct underlined file, folder and restored file on the same SPA document in all six width/theme combinations after each destination settled. The focused Copy and its clipboard payload were also tested across navigation. Mobile drawer and desktop graph returned focus, and Search returned to its opener in each of my six states. |
| 20 · Font preferences and transitions | Reject the first candidate. My browser trace measured a −33.2px horizontal gap during 16→32px font growth when Copy resized immediately and Expand interpolated its position and width. The published baseline stayed at or above 4.8px. In the corrected build the adjacent controls adopted their new geometry together. Browser-default changes in both directions at 390, 900 and 1440px showed 4.8px or 9.6px clearance. Expand retains its hover-opacity transition in normal motion, and both controls compute to 0s under reduced motion. |

The existing graph-mode change triggers Quartz's render lifecycle. On clean direct loads at 390 and 900px all six Azure Documentation diagrams rendered. Crossing that breakpoint in either direction replaced all six with a Mermaid syntax-error graphic, which persisted after crossing back. This reproduced against the accepted implementation and the corrected component presentation. This behavior was present on direct comparison with the accepted build before the stylesheet change. The authored source remains intact for Copy. The renderer's repeat initialization, redundant clipboard controls in the DOM, hidden graph simulation and dialog focus/label behavior need component-level work. The Linux browser results leave physical-device behavior and screen-reader speech unverified.


## Verification and scoring

The full build emitted 913 files and all 164 automated tests passed. The scoped stylesheet formatter passed. The repository-wide checker still exits on the two previously documented TypeScript dependency errors for `micromorph` and `remark-parse/lib`.

The route measurements compared the 161-path sets and both horizontal bounds for main content and titles at each width. Separately, Chrome, Brave and Microsoft Edge each ran ten combinations of viewport, theme and browser font size on five representative pages, yielding 150 page layouts and 30 Search states. I also inspected the final preview directly on Home, Blog, an article, the Explorer drawer, Search, the live desktop graph and the two affected diagram controls. Native browser preference changes and opening the graph used separate routes from the static corpus crawl.

The overall score remains **8.525/10** under the publication audit weights. In the established order, the final scores are 9 editorial design, 9 typography, 8.5 CSS, 9 themes, 9 responsive behavior, 7.5 Quartz integration, 8.5 technical content and tables, 7.5 accessibility, and 7.5 motion and performance. The weights are 15%, 15%, 15%, 15%, 10%, 10%, 5%, 10% and 5%. I raised accessibility by half a point on the evidence of a persistent current-location cue and a single keyboard Copy stop. I lowered Quartz integration by half a point because breakpoint changes can destroy six valid drawings on one article. These adjustments offset one another. The retained typography, palette and rails, expanded test coverage, and passing tests justify no additional points.

**Signed by the independent Design Director.** The decision applies to local build `index-0731cabb.css` after correction and independent reassessment. Further visual changes need new evidence. The component-level Mermaid and clipboard lifecycle issues remain open for a separately authorized change.
